response.rationale: R3 is the only syndrome-level label directly matched by the decisive raw span of both great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle. R7 quotes the same span but mislabels it as Tetralogy of Fallot; TOF requires an overriding aorta and pulmonary outflow obstruction, neither of which is in the vignette. The hypoplastic left ventricle, reduced mitral orifice, VSD, ASD, and tricuspid regurgitation fit a Double Outlet Right Ventricle complex better than TOF or isolated component diagnoses.

rejected.why: Right heart dilation and tricuspid regurgitation are nonspecific; no apical tricuspid displacement or atrialized right ventricle is present, and the parallel great-vessel origin points to DORV.
Severe tricuspid regurgitation implies a patent tricuspid valve, contradicting tricuspid atresia; the hypoplastic left ventricle and mitral orifice are part of the DORV complex.
Ventricular septal defect alone is a component finding and does not explain the two parallel great vessels arising from the right ventricle.
Atrial septal defect alone is a component finding and does not explain the VSD or parallel great-vessel origin.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a secondary Doppler finding, not a primary diagnosis; it leaves the great-vessel origin and septal defects unexplained.
Correlated completion of R3 using the same raw span; it adds no independent evidence once restatements are discounted.
Append-only completion of ASD; too narrow to represent the composite Double Outlet Right Ventricle diagnosis.
Append-only completion of VSD; too narrow and lacks the decisive great-vessel origin.
Append-only completion of tricuspid regurgitation; same limitation as R2 and not a diagnostic entity.
